definitions.explanation: The son of one's sibling. Used for both the son of a brother and the son of a sister.

examples.japanese: {甥|おい}が{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}た。
{甥|おい}は{今年|ことし}{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入学|にゅうがく}する。
examples.english: My nephew will start elementary school this year.

examples.japanese: {姉|あね}の{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}が{大|おお}きくなって、もう{高校生|こうこうせい}になった。
examples.english: My sister's nephew has grown up and is already a high school student.

notes:
USAGE:
When referring to one's own nephew in polite conversation, use {甥|おい} or the more casual {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}. When referring to someone else's nephew politely, use {甥御|おいご}さん.

RELATED WORDS:
- {姪|めい}: niece
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}: nephew (casual, affectionate)
- {甥御|おいご}さん: someone else's nephew (polite)

KANJI NOTE:
The kanji {甥|おい} is a single-kanji word. Also sometimes written {甥|おい}っ{子|こ} in casual speech, which adds a diminutive, affectionate nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}: nephew (casual)
- {甥御|おいご}さん: nephew (polite, about others' nephews)
- {甥|おい}{姪|めい}: nephews and nieces
